action.question: How far should the history-rewrite worker go?

questions.question: How far should the history-rewrite worker go?

options.label: Prepare-only, then surface for review (Recommended)
options.description: Worker clones FamilyFund into a scratch mirror, runs filter-repo to redact the blob, verifies via gitleaks that all history is clean, produces a backup of the pre-rewrite state, and stops. Manager + owner review the rewritten mirror. Then a separate one-shot dispatch does the force-push. Safest staging.

options.label: Full rewrite + force-push origin in one go
options.description: Worker does the whole thing: rewrite, verify, force-push origin main (and clean up dependabot refs that branch from old SHAs), then re-run the SOP audit. Faster end-to-end. Main is not branch-protected yet (#54 is scheduled for post-sync), so the push is mechanically possible — but it's a one-way operation on shared state.

options.label: Rewrite + force-push + ALSO rotate mail password as part of same worker
options.description: Adds the deploy-track item to the worker's scope: confirm/rotate the leaked MAIL_PASSWORD on spirit, document in SECRET-ROTATION-RUNBOOK, then proceed with the rewrite + push. Biggest scope; touches prod.

questions.question: What about the leaked mail password itself? (Independent from rewrite path.)

options.label: File it as a deploy-track task under FF#20 (do not do now)
options.description: Adds the mail-password rotation as a sub-item of the existing FF#20 (prod secret rotation) ticket. Tracked but separate from this public-track work. Recommended if you trust the value is currently dormant or rotation is queued already.

options.label: Investigate first — is the leaked value still live?
options.description: Quick check: pull the current prod MAIL_PASSWORD from secrets repo / spirit and compare to the leaked blob. If different, rotation already happened (close cleanly). If same, urgent.

options.label: Rotate now as a parallel deploy-track task
options.description: Spin a separate worker to drive the rotation: change the prod SMTP credential, update SOPS+age secrets, deploy. Independent of history rewrite. Highest urgency interpretation.

## What the BLOCK actually means

The worker's framing was slightly off, which I caught by inspecting the artifacts directly. The truth:

- **Current HEAD is clean.** Line 52 at `3133c039` (today's HEAD) is just `# MAIL_PASSWORD_ENCRYPTED=` — empty placeholder. A later commit scrubbed the value.
- **Commit `22b12844` (2026-05-22) is dirty.** This is the *security cleanup commit itself* — `security(dev): untrack leaked .env.dev, add .env.example template + rotation docs`. The cleanup commit shipped its own `.env.example` with a real **251-char encrypted `MAIL_PASSWORD_ENCRYPTED=eyJ...`** blob in it. The fix commit was its own incident.
- **gitleaks-HEAD vs gitleaks-ALL.** `gitleaks detect` without `--no-git` walks history by default (not the working tree), so both scans found the same single fingerprint at 22b12844. The blob is **history-only.**

## Why this is FF#10-blocking under Option 6a

FF was decided 6a (mirror push of full history) back on 2026-05-28 because rounds 1+2 audited history clean. The strict SOP config caught what those audits missed. Pushing full history exposes `22b12844`'s blob to the public.

## The mail-password rotation question (deploy-track adjacent)

That commit's message says APP_KEY was rotated + sessions invalidated. **It says nothing about the leaked mail password.** If never rotated, that's also a deploy-track incident — `MAIL_PASSWORD_ENCRYPTED` may still authenticate against the prod SMTP today.
History rewrite it is. One more decision before I dispatch the worker — this involves a force-push to `main`, so I want explicit scope.
